statecraft.title: Who held which areas, 1948-49: the front lines of ISA 6158/1 and, from each agreement's date, the sides of the 1949 armistice lines (true polygons, not hex-snapped)
statecraft.review: owner-verify (sensitivity review before a shareable build)
statecraft.licence: CC-BY-SA-4.0 (content/); facts redrawn by our own method from the sources below, no image copied
statecraft.meaning: Military control on a date (owner ruling 2026-10-14), nothing else: not sovereignty, ownership or population. From each armistice the side of the agreement's line, which the agreements themselves say is not a political or territorial boundary (Egypt Art. V.2; Jordan Art. VI.9).

sources.cite: Israel State Archives, Prime Minister's Office, Government Secretariat, map 6158/1, file 'פלשתינה - קווי החלוקה וקווי החזית' (Palestine: the partition lines and the front lines), 1949, marked secret; a Survey of Palestine 1:250,000 'Palestine: Index to Villages & Settlements' sheet with the lines drawn by hand. ISA id ISA-PMO-GovernmentSecretary-R0005czg. The copy used: NYU Faculty Digital Archive, Jewish Settlements Archival Project, PDF page 2 (2368 x 4078 px).
sources.licence: A 1949 Israeli state work: out of copyright in Israel (Copyright Act 2007 s. 42); a possible URAA US term in its drawing does not reach the facts taken (where a front line ran on a date); its base is a Survey of Palestine sheet (D-B). Facts only, redrawn by our own method; no image is copied.

sources.cite: UN General Assembly Resolution 181 (II), 29 November 1947, Part II, Boundaries (the Avalon Project text): used only to tell the partition line (not traced) from the green front line where they run close.
S/1025, the Mediator's report on the observation of the truce (11 June - 9 July 1948): the Jerusalem agreement of 16 June, an agreed line with a no-man's land between the two lines.

CIA, Near East/Africa Branch, Intelligence Summary Vol. III No. 19, week ending 19 May 1948, page 2: 'Military Situation - 18 May 1948', map no. 10981 (Map Branch, CIA, 4-48), CONFIDENTIAL, declassified and approved for release 2013-07-22. Legend: 'Border of strongly-held Jewish area' (heavy solid line), 'Border of tenuously-held Jewish area' (heavy dashed line). Record CIA-RDP78-01617A004700010003-6; the copy used: the Wayback Machine's of the reading room PDF, page 2 (1594 x 2108 px, 1 bit).
sources.licence: A US federal government work, not protected by US copyright (17 USC 105); its 1:250,000 base is a UK military sheet (facts only, as D-B). Facts only, redrawn by our own method; no image is copied.

searched_for_a_better_copy: Israel State Archives catalogue page (the ISA link above) and catalog.archives.gov.il: HTTP 403 (CloudFront) to a plain client on 2026-10-14; not reached.
Wikimedia Commons (API file searches '6158/1', 'קווי החזית', 'קווי החלוקה וקווי החזית', 'R0005czg', 'front lines 1948 Israel State Archives map', 'הפוגה הראשונה מפה'): no copy.
NYU Faculty Digital Archive record 2451/72921 (full record): one file, the PDF used (the map at 2368 x 4078 px).

the 1950 modus vivendi line: it does not change either side's position (S/1471 Art. III)
the CIA 18 May 1948 map's strongly-held (solid) border: on the greyscale scan it cannot be told from the partition boundary, the roads and the railway (research note control-15-may-1948.md section 9)

the CIA 18 May map's dashed (tenuously held) border along the Jerusalem corridor: legible, but a single line along the road that closes on no sourced line; its area is cut by the Jerusalem sub-district instead

the CIA 18 May map's dashed (tenuously held) border by Rishon-Sarafand: legible, but it runs into the lettering by Jaffa and closes on no sourced line; not drawn (owner ruling 2 of 16 October 2026 on #686: in the Ramle sub-district only Yibna's hex is grey, Rehovot and Rishon stay blue)
the CIA 18 May map's dashed loop by the north Dead Sea works: not legible on this copy (one dash, then the 'Palestine Potash Ltd' lettering); the area keeps the 9 July line's side
the CIA 18 May map's dashed border from Ramle to Latrun: within about 1.5 km of the 9 July line all the way (below both maps' accuracy)
known_staleness: the October 1948 line is shown until the Egypt agreement (24 February 1949), since no source gives a later line: Isdud (taken 28 October), Majdal (4-5 November) and Yad Mordechai stay on the other side until then; the caption names the source line's date

15 May - 10 June 1948 is one period on the 9 July lines (owner ruling Q4, #674): changes inside it are not shown by day: Atarot (17 May) and Neve Yaakov (18 May) evacuated, the Kinarot valley fighting (18-22 May), Kalia and Beit HaArava abandoned (20 May), Yad Mordechai fallen (24 May; its hex stays blue), RAF Ramat David handed over (26 May), the Jewish Quarter surrendered (28 May), Isdud taken by the Egyptian army (29 May), Nitzanim fallen (7 June), Mishmar HaYarden taken by the Syrian army (10 June); and the British evacuation enclave at Haifa (to 30 June 1948) is not drawn (owner ruling Q5: an info-panel note)

the south in 15 May - 10 June 1948: only the Jewish settlements whose 1948 site the repository holds are pinned blue (Yad Mordechai, Negba, Nir Am, Dorot, Shoval, Mishmar HaNegev, Hatzerim, Nevatim); Nitzanim, Kfar Darom, Nirim, Be'erot Yitzhak and others are not, their sites having moved after 1948 with no 1948 site sourced here; Revivim, south of the 60-km northing, stays without colour as in every 1948 period

Huleiqat: ISA 6158/1's lines put it on the Israeli side from 9 July 1948, but en.wiki has Egypt retake it on 8 July and Israel capture it on 19 October 1948 (Operation Yoav); its hex is pinned to Egypt for 8 July - 19 October (pinned_towns). A known limit of the periods: the pin covers whole periods inside its window, so the Yoav period (15-29 October) shows the hex Israeli from 15 October, four days before its capture

contested_places.why: Yibna, occupied by the Givati Brigade on 5 June 1948 (en.wiki Yibna, revision 1375084946)
Acre: Operation Ben-Ami from 13 May; attacked on 16 May, the town surrendered on the night of 17/18 May 1948 (en.wiki Acre, Israel, revision 1380244094; Operation Ben-Ami, revision 1369980718)

pinned_towns.why: taken by the Syrian army in June 1948 and back in Israel's control on 20 July 1949 (en.wiki); the bridgehead is narrower than ISA 6158/1's accuracy, so its lines put the moshava on the Israeli side

read 2026-10-14: en.wiki quotes Sami Hadawi, who argues that the 1949 armistice lines severed the town's orange groves in favour of Israel, leaving it its rocky land to the east, which implies the town stayed on the Jordanian side (an inference, not a statement of the source); on the signed map 1 of the Jordan-Israel agreement (the UNISPAL copy D-A traced, 51 m a pixel) the pen line runs along the town's western edge, its symbol on or just east of the line, which that resolution cannot settle; D-A's trace of it puts the town 2 km to the Israeli side from 8 May 1949

retaken by the Egyptian army on 8 July 1948 and captured by the Giv'ati Brigade on 19 October 1948 in Operation Yoav (en.wiki); ISA 6158/1's 9 July line puts it on the Israeli side, about 1.3 km from the line, so the source and the archive map disagree for these weeks

closures.jerusalem: The Jordan line stops at the city's western edge on both sides (map 2, the 30 November 1948 cease-fire lines, is not available: D-A). The 1948 lines within 4.5 km of Jerusalem (ISA 6158/1, July 1948) stay to close it; the hexes that hold both sides there are grey (no-man's land: S/1025; Art. V.1(b)).
closures.egypt_south: The 1949 Egypt line is drawn from the Wadi Hasi to Gaza only (D-A gap). It is closed straight from its end to the frontier at the middle of the N 70-72 km stretch that Art. VI.3 bounds; the land within 3 km of that straight stretch has no colour (no sourced line).

periods.why: owner decision of 16 October 2026 (#674, option b, '9 July lines, adjusted'): no line for 15 May can be traced honestly, so the 9 July line with grey where the front moved before 11 June or the CIA's 18 May map shows a tenuous hold, the south without colour (its settlements blue), Jerusalem no-man's land (research note control-15-may-1948.md section 9)
the first truce: the line ISA 6158/1 dates 9 July 1948, the closest sourced line (owner ruling 2026-10-14)
the October line stands until the Egypt agreement: no source gives a later line (Operation Horev is not drawn)
